description: Are my backups encrypted? What happens to an old backup when I add or change the namespace password?

conversation.content: Are my backups encrypted? What happens to an old backup when I add or change the namespace password?

criteria.instruction: Explain the encrypted/plaintext snapshot distinction and readable outer archive/metadata; do not describe all backups as encrypted or their protection as unknown.

Explain unchanged historical backups, including old plaintext backups after adding protection and original snapshot password after a password change. No automatic archive rewrite or new-password guarantee.

expectation.reference_facts: A backup copies the notes and files SQLite snapshots, without decrypting their encrypted payloads, into a gzip tar archive with a readable manifest. Protected snapshots retain sensitive ciphertext and the wrapped DEK; a plaintext snapshot remains plaintext. Outer archive/manifest/structural metadata are not all encrypted. Existing archives are immutable; adding a password does not encrypt old plaintext backups; changing a password does not rewrap old backup keys. Restoring an encrypted archive needs the password for that snapshot. Source archives are never rewritten.
